claim: Prenatal exposure raises adult open-field activity: the mean activity score of offspring of exposed dams is higher than that of offspring of control dams, and a two-sample t test of the difference between the two group means gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: open-field activity score (distance travelled, arbitrary units) measured in adulthood on each pup of each dam
whether the dam received the exposure during pregnancy

sizes: dams = 20; pups = 8 (activity: 20 x 8 = 160 values; exposed: 20 values)

claim: The compound raises the share of cells that respond to stimulation: the proportion of responding cells is higher in treated wells than in untreated wells, and a test of the difference between the two groups gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: whether each imaged cell of each well showed a calcium response to the stimulus
whether the well was given the compound before stimulation

sizes: wells = 12; cells = 150 (responded: 12 x 150 = 1800 values; treated: 12 values)

claim: Spine density on hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons rises with the dose of the drug the animal received: the regression slope of spine density on dose is positive, and a test of the slope gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: spines per 10 micrometres of dendrite on each sampled neuron, in each histological section, of each animal
dose of the drug (mg/kg) that each animal received

sizes: animals = 12; sections = 4; neurons = 25 (spine_density: 12 x 4 x 25 = 1200 values; dose: 12 values)

claim: Giving the compound in the drinking water reduces body-weight gain: the mean weight gain of animals receiving the compound is lower than that of controls, and a Welch two-sample t test of the difference between the two group means gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: body-weight gain in grams over the study of each animal housed in each cage
whether the drinking water supplied to the cage contained the compound

sizes: cages = 40; animals = 2 (weight_gain: 40 x 2 = 80 values; treated: 40 values)

claim: The training programme improves task accuracy more than the control activity: the mean change in accuracy (post minus pre) is larger in the trained group than in the control group, and a two-sample t test of the difference between the two groups' mean changes gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: task accuracy (proportion correct) of each subject before the programme
task accuracy (proportion correct) of each subject after the programme
whether the subject took part in the training programme (true) or in the control activity (false)

sizes: subjects = 40 (pre, post and trained: 40 values each)

claim: Reaction times fall more steeply over practice sessions in healthy subjects than in patients: the mean per-subject linear slope of reaction time on session number is more negative in the healthy group, and a two-sample t test of the difference between the two groups' mean slopes gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: median reaction time in milliseconds of each subject in each practice session, sessions in order
whether the subject belongs to the patient group (true) or the healthy group (false)

sizes: subjects = 30; sessions = 8 (rt: 30 x 8 = 240 values; patient: 30 values)

claim: The task engages region A more than region B: the task-evoked signal change (task minus rest) is larger in region A than in region B, with the mean across subjects of the within-subject difference of the two signal changes positive, and a paired t test of that difference gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: mean signal in region A of each subject during task blocks (percent signal change units)
mean signal in region A of each subject during rest blocks
mean signal in region B of each subject during task blocks
mean signal in region B of each subject during rest blocks

sizes: subjects = 24 (each of the four keys: 24 values)

claim: The insecticide lowers invertebrate density: the mean density in treated tanks is lower than in control tanks, and a Welch two-sample t test of the difference between the two group means gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: invertebrates per litre counted in each of the water samples taken from each tank
whether the tank received the insecticide

sizes: tanks = 8; samples = 10 (density: 8 x 10 = 80 values; treated: 8 values)

claim: The treatment raises invertebrate abundance in the field plots: abundance is higher in treated plots than in control plots, and a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test comparing the abundances of the two groups gives p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: number of individuals counted in a sample from each plot on each weekly sampling date, dates in order
whether the plot received the treatment

sizes: plots = 12; dates = 12 (abundance: 12 x 12 = 144 values; treated: 12 values)

claim: The drug improves motor coordination: the mean time spent on the rotarod is longer in the treatment group than in the control group, and a two-tailed two-sample t test of the difference between the two group means gives p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: time in seconds that each rat stayed on the rotarod on each of the consecutive test days
whether the rat was in the treatment group (true) or the control group (false)

sizes: rats = 10; days = 3 (latency: 10 x 3 = 30 values; treated: 10 values)

claim: Across subjects, mean resting heart rate and mean salivary cortisol (each subject's mean over the recording days) are positively correlated: the Pearson correlation between the two subject means is positive, and a test of that correlation gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: resting heart rate in beats per minute of each subject on each recording day
morning salivary cortisol concentration of each subject on each recording day

sizes: subjects = 16; days = 10 (heart_rate and cortisol: 16 x 10 = 160 values each)

claim: Scores on the task and on the symptom scale are more strongly related in group A than in group B: the Pearson correlation between task score and symptom score is higher in group A than in group B, and a Fisher z test of the difference between the two correlations gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: score of each participant on the experimental task
score of each participant on the symptom questionnaire
whether the participant belongs to group A (true) or group B (false)

sizes: participants = 40 (each of the three keys: 40 values)
